Madison website design has to keep up with a town that runs on seasons and semesters. A vegetable farmer sells on the Capitol Square from spring into November, a shop on Williamson Street sees students scatter for summer and a new class arrive each fall, and a landscaper's phone goes quiet when the snow comes. Each of them needs a site that says what is happening right now, not last year.

Dominion Web Design Pro builds those sites. Maurice Johnson writes every page by hand, you see a free demo before any invoice, and the price is printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, one time.

Saturday on the Square, and the other six days

The Dane County Farmers' Market sets up around the Capitol Square on Saturday mornings from April to November, and it is widely described as the largest producer-only farmers' market in the country. The rule is simple: everything for sale is grown, raised or made in Wisconsin by the person behind the stand. For 2026 the Saturday season runs April 11 to November 14, and a Wednesday market runs on Martin Luther King Jr. Boulevard. Because vendors sell only what they produce, popular items can sell out before closing.

That last point is where a website earns its keep. A shopper who missed your eggs on Saturday wants to know how else to buy them. A farm or food maker's site can answer that the rest of the week.

  1. Where to find youWhich market days you attend, which side of the Square, and any weeks you skip.
  2. What is in seasonA short list you send over when it changes, updated as part of maintenance.
  3. How to buy between marketsCSA shares, farm pickup, restaurant and wholesale inquiries, each going to your inbox through the contact form.
  4. Who you areThe farm, the family, the town, and photos of the actual fields or kitchen.

A capital, a campus and a software giant next door

Madison had about 286,000 people in 2025, Wisconsin's second largest city after Milwaukee, in a metro area of about 710,000. Three big employers shape who your customers are.

State government

The Capitol sits in the middle of the Square, so downtown fills with government workers and visitors on weekdays. Lunch spots, printers and services within a short walk get searched by people who only have an hour.

UW-Madison

The university enrolled nearly 52,000 students in fall 2025, including an incoming class of 8,500. Newcomers know few neighborhood names, so they search by what they need and how close it is.

Epic in Verona

The health care software company employs around 13,000 people, most of them at its Verona campus. People who move for jobs like these still have to pick a dentist, a barber and a mechanic, and most start with a search.

Web design Madison WI neighborhoods make sense of

The east side has a long habit of backing its own shops. On Williamson Street, which locals call Willy Street, locally owned shops, restaurants and music venues have filled storefronts that once sat empty, and the American Planning Association credits neighbors with pushing back against chain development. The Willy Street Co-op grocery opened in 1974 and added a second store in Middleton in 2010. Atwood Avenue runs east from Williamson toward Schenk-Atwood, with its own row of local shops and cafes.

Customers in Madison talk in places like these: Willy Street, Atwood, Monroe Street, State Street, and suburbs such as Middleton and Fitchburg. If your shop is on one of those streets, the street name belongs in your page title and first paragraph, plainly.

For trades that cover the whole county

A lawn crew, roofer or auto shop does not sell from a market stall. It sells trust and a short drive. Google says local results turn on relevance, distance and prominence, so a site that names the towns you work in and the services you offer in plain words gives it more to match. A Fitchburg homeowner searching for spring cleanup wants to see Fitchburg on your page, along with photos of real jobs and a phone number that dials with one tap.

For most single-location shops, Starter at $497 is enough: five pages, live in 7 to 14 days. Pro at $997 adds city pages for crews that cover several towns; its AI chat widget is free for 14 days, then $297 a month. Agency at $1,997 starts with keyword research, then builds a page for each town and service worth having, first pages live inside two weeks. It includes AI phone agent setup; the agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time, and is not part of the one-time price. We do not sell page counts.

Dane County help that costs little or nothing

  • Wisconsin SBDC at UW-Madison. No-cost, confidential consulting on planning, financing, marketing and management, mainly for owners in Dane, Sauk and Columbia counties.
  • City of Madison Office of Business Resources. Steers owners to city and outside financial and technical help, guides them through permits, and runs programs such as facade grants, 0% KIVA Madison loans and commercial ownership assistance. Owners working with partners such as the Madison Black Chamber of Commerce can get an extra Kiva match.

Wisconsin is full of businesses this size. The SBA Office of Advocacy's 2025 profile counts 497,370 small businesses in the state, 99.4% of all businesses, employing 48.0% of Wisconsin's workers.

Common questions

How do I find a good website designer in Madison, WI?

Look at what you would actually get, not a slideshow of other people's work. Ask who writes the page copy, what the first year costs in total, how changes are handled and who owns the site. We answer those in writing before you buy: Maurice Johnson writes and builds the site, the prices are one time, you own it, and you see a free demo built for your business first. He works remotely from East Texas, not from an office in Madison.

How much does Madison website design cost?

Ours costs $497 for Starter, five pages live in 7 to 14 days; $997 for Pro, ten pages plus ten city pages; or $1,997 for Agency, which starts with keyword research across your whole area. All are one-time prices. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent. The AI chat widget (Pro) or phone agent (Agency) is $297 a month after its free trial, and you can skip it. Other designers may bill hourly or monthly, so compare the full first-year total.

Does my web help have to be in Madison?

No. Most of the work on a small business site happens by phone, email and shared links whoever you hire. What matters is that the designer asks about your business and writes the pages for it. A local designer can meet you for coffee; we cannot. In exchange you get printed prices and a free demo before any commitment.

Can a farm website take CSA sign-ups or sell online?

A contact form can take CSA interest, wholesale inquiries and pickup requests and email each one to you, and that is in every package. A full online store with a cart and payments is not part of our packages. If you need one, tell us when you ask for the demo and we will be honest about whether we are the right fit.

Do you write pages for Middleton, Fitchburg or Verona customers?

Yes, when you really work there. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each one researched and written for that town, which suits a landscaper or cleaner who covers several Dane County communities. A shop with one door on Monroe Street usually only needs Starter.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
